title: Ready a wheelchair for a transfer: swing both legrests away and lock both wheel brakes
instruction: Get the wheelchair ready for a transfer: swing both legrests away and put both brakes on.
context: Locking both wheel brakes and swinging both legrests away before a transfer is a core safety step for nursing assistants (about 1.35 million US workers, BLS OEWS May 2023). The difficulty is physical: four separate mechanisms, two per arm. Each legrest is a hinged hanger swung out through a 90-degree arc about its vertical hinge by pushing its release handle round from the seat side; each brake is a lever pushed forward 25 degrees onto the tyre. Each arm works its own side; the two legrests meet in the middle, so the arms must take turns there.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the point midway between the two arm bases, which stand 61 cm apart: forward means away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. Wheelchair (wheelchair, fixed): parked facing the arms, centred 27 cm forward on the centre line; seat 17 cm wide at 7 cm; two 12 cm rear wheels 10 cm either side; front casters. Legrests (legrest_left, legrest_right joints): grey hangers 7 cm wide and 6 cm tall with footplates and a 4 cm release handle standing at the free end (reaching 11 cm up, above the seat), in front of the seat, each hinged on a vertical axis at the seat's outer front corner (18.5 cm forward, 8.5 cm either side), swinging out towards the arms (friction 0.05 N m); their free edges meet 1.5 cm either side of the centre line. Brakes (brake_left, brake_right joints): red levers 5 cm tall with a knob, 25 cm forward, 11.2 cm either side, pivoting forward onto the tyres (friction 0.08 N m), off when upright. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: A legrest is swung away when its hinge has turned at least 80 degrees out; a brake is on when its lever has been pushed at least 25 degrees forward onto the tyre. Score at the end of the trial: 0.2 per legrest swung away and per brake on (0 to 0.8). 1.0 when all four are done, nothing moves (under 0.03 rad over the last 0.3 s) and no gripper tool point is within 4 cm of a brake lever's knob, held for 1 s (the trial then ends; completed less than 1 s before the run limit scores 0.8).
reset_notes: Swing both legrests back in front of the seat and stand both brake levers upright (off).
fidelity: Approximate. The wheelchair is fixed to the table and reduced to rigid boxes and cylinders; legrests and brakes are friction-held hinges (the brakes' over-centre detent and the legrests' release catch are not modelled); brake engagement is judged by lever angle. PhysX rigid-body contacts with default friction.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (neither legrest swung away and neither brake set; hit the 120 s step limit); demo: 1.0 (both brake levers pushed onto the tyres and both legrests swung out of the way by their release handles, one arm at a time at the legrests' meeting edges; hands clear, held 1 s)
